title: Battery policy
text: Robots must return to charge when the battery falls below 18 percent. A full charge takes 95 minutes on a Type C dock. Batteries are replaced after 1,200 charge cycles.

title: Speed limits
text: The maximum robot speed is 1.6 metres per second in open zones. In aisles the limit is 0.8 metres per second. In the cold store the limit drops to 0.5 metres per second because floors may be icy.

title: Incident reporting
text: Any collision must be reported to the shift supervisor within 15 minutes. Serious incidents go to the safety lead, Amara Okafor. Incident records are retained for 7 years.

title: Shift patterns
text: The day shift starts at 06:00. The night shift starts at 18:00. Handover meetings last 20 minutes. Each shift has one supervisor per 12 technicians.

title: Protective equipment
text: Steel-toe boots and high-visibility vests are required on the floor. Hearing protection is required only in the compressor room. Visitors receive a temporary badge valid for 8 hours.

title: Software releases
text: Fleet software is released on the second Tuesday of each month. A canary is deployed to 5 percent of robots for 48 hours. Rollback must finish within 30 minutes if the error rate exceeds 2 percent.

title: Maintenance schedule
text: Wheels are inspected every 500 operating hours. LiDAR sensors are recalibrated every 90 days. Maintenance logs are stored in the Atlas system.

title: Payload limits
text: The maximum payload of the M3 robot is 140 kilograms. The larger M5 robot carries up to 320 kilograms. Loads above 300 kilograms require two-person sign-off.

title: Customer returns
text: Customers may return goods within 28 days of delivery. Refunds are issued within 5 working days. Damaged goods are sent to bay 14 for inspection.

title: Cold store working
text: The cold store is kept at minus 18 degrees Celsius. Staff may work inside for at most 45 minutes before taking a break of 15 minutes.

title: Fire safety
text: The fire assembly point is car park B. Fire drills take place every 6 months. Robots halt automatically when the fire alarm sounds.

title: Network
text: Robots connect to the private 5G network named depot-core. If the network is lost for more than 10 seconds, a robot stops and waits. Wi-Fi is used only in the office block.

title: Data retention
text: Camera footage is kept for 30 days and then deleted. Access to footage requires approval from the data protection officer, Lena Fischer. Telemetry is retained for 13 months.

title: Training
text: New technicians complete a 3-week induction. Forklift certification must be renewed every 3 years. First aid refresher courses run every January.

title: Expenses
text: Travel claims must be submitted within 60 days. Hotel costs are capped at 140 pounds per night in London and 95 pounds elsewhere. The meal allowance is 25 pounds per day.

title: Annual leave
text: Employees receive 27 days of annual leave plus bank holidays. Up to 5 days may carry over to the next year. Requests over 10 days need director approval.

title: Stock control
text: Full stock counts happen each quarter. Cycle counts cover 2 percent of locations daily. Variances above 0.5 percent are escalated to the inventory manager.

title: Loading docks
text: Dock doors 1 to 6 are for inbound lorries and doors 7 to 12 are for outbound lorries. Drivers must book a slot 24 hours in advance. A late arrival loses its slot after 30 minutes.

title: Emergency stops
text: Red emergency stop buttons are mounted every 25 metres along aisles. After an emergency stop, a restart requires a technician's key. The buttons are tested each week.

title: Suppliers
text: The LiDAR supplier is Ardent Optics. Wheel assemblies come from Kestrel Drives. Purchase orders above 10,000 pounds need finance approval.
